Judgment :
1. These three appeals are preferred against the judgments and orders passed by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Thane (for short "the Tribunal").
2. The issues involved in all these appeals are same, hence, I am deciding these appeals by this common judgment.
3. It is contention of learned counsel for the appellant-Insurance Company that respondent No.1-claimant is daughter of deceased in First Appeal Nos.1432 and 1601 of 2016 and sister of deceased in First Appeal No.1394 of 2016.

Learned counsel further submitted that the Reliance General Insurance Co. Ltd vs Smt. Divya Alok Srivastav And Anr. on 7 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/193078697/
2 claimant was married, hence, she cannot be considered as dependent of the deceased but this fact is not considered by the Tribunal and requested to allow the appeal.
4. Though respondents are served, none present for respondents.
5. The appeals are of the year 2016, hence, I am deciding these appeals on merit.

sentences.text: 6. I have heard learned counsel for the appellant-Insurance Company, perused the judgments and orders passed by the Tribunal.
2/4  ::: Uploaded on - 14/07/2025 ::: Downloaded on - 01/08/2025 23:07:21   Shubhada S Kadam 65-FA-1432-2016-Judgment.doc 7.
The issues raised by learned counsel for the appellant- Insurance Company is about dependency of the married daughter.
As per Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (for short "the M.V.Act"), legal representatives can file claim petition.

Under Section 166 of the M.V. Act,
the term "dependent" is not mentioned and only there is reference of legal representatives.

While deciding this issue, the learned Tribunal has observed that the claimant is daughter of deceased in in First Appeal Nos.1432 and 1601 of 2016 and sister of deceased in First Appeal No.1394 of 2016 and she is legal representative of deceased
, on that ground, the Tribunal has awarded compensation.
I do not find infirmity in it.
In my view, the legal representatives can claim compensation on behalf of deceased irrespective of the fact whether married or not.

8. In view of above, the appeals are devoid of merit and I pass following order :
